extracted.intended_audience: users of the PARI/GP library (computational number theorists, mathematicians and developers using PARI/GP)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP number-field, class-field, Galois and ideal-related library functions: describes function semantics, outputs, flags, preconditions, return formats, and usage notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrdisc / bnrdisc0 output semantics and flags
rubrics_metrics.description: When producing absolute data related to L/Q: N is the absolute degree [L : Q], r1 the number of real places of L, and D the discriminant of L/Q. Otherwise, for relative data L/K: N is the relative degree [L : K], r1 is the number of real places of K unramified in L (so number of real places of L equals r1 times N), and D is the relative discriminant ideal of L/K. If bit 2 of the flag is set and the modulus is not the conductor of L, only return 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN bnrdisc0(GEN A, GEN B = NULL, GEN C = NULL, long flag). Use the flag bits to control whether absolute or relative data are returned and to restrict output to conductors (bit 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrdisclist output format and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes a list of discriminants of Abelian extensions of the number field by increasing modulus norm up to bound. Output v is a vector of vectors where v[i][j] corresponds to entries of a single big vector V; each V[k] is a vector W indexed by ideals of norm k. When arch is specified, components are [m, d, r, D] (m = prime ideal factorization of modulus, d = [L:Q], r = number of real places of L, D = absolute discriminant factorization). If arch omitted, components are [m, [[d1,r1,D1],..., [dt,rt,Dt]]]. Prime ideal pr = [p, α, e, f, β] is coded as p*n2 + (f-1)*n + (j-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN bnrdisclist(GEN bnf, GEN bound, GEN arch = NULL). Use bnrdecodemodule to decode m. For a single field prefer bnrclassno or bnrdisc for efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrgaloisapply: apply automorphism matrix to congruence subgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the automorphism given by its matrix mat to the congruence subgroup H given as a HNF matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN bnrgaloisapply(GEN bnr, GEN mat, GEN H). Matrix mat can be computed with bnrgaloismatrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrgaloismatrix: matrix of automorphism action on generators
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the matrix of the action of an automorphism aut of the base field bnf.nf on the generators of the ray class field bnr.gen. aut can be a polynomial, algebraic number, vector of automorphisms or a Galois group (then a vector of matrices is returned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN bnrgaloismatrix(GEN bnr, GEN aut). For polynomial/algebraic number use bnrautmatrix. See bnrisgalois for example; precomputing matrices can save repeated recomputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrinit: initialize ray class (bnr) structure and flag behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: bnf (including fundamental units) and f (modulus) initialize data linked to the ray class group structure (bnr). Result members: .bnf (underlying bnf), .mod (modulus), .bid (bid structure), .clgp/.no/.cyc/.gen (ray class group, cardinality, elementary divisors, generators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag = 0 (default) generators are not computed (saves time) and accessing bnr.gen causes an error. If flag = 1 generators are computed. Rather than numeric flags, prefer GEN Buchray(GEN bnf, GEN module, long flag) using nf_GEN and nf_INIT constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrisconductor: conductors check
rubrics_metrics.description: Fast variant of bnrconductor; outputs 1 if the modulus is the conductor, 0 otherwise. Slightly faster when the character or subgroup is not primitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long bnrisconductor0(GEN A, GEN B = NULL, GEN C = NULL). Use when you only need a boolean conductor check.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrisgalois: check class field Galois property over subfield
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether the class field attached to subgroup H is Galois over the subfield of bnr.nf fixed by group gal (gal can be as from galoisinit, a matrix, or vector of matrices). The function assumes the ray class field attached to bnr is Galois (this is not checked).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long bnrisgalois(GEN bnr, GEN gal, GEN H). Precompute bnrgaloismatrix(B,G) and pass matrices (second option) to avoid repeated recomputation and improve speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrisprincipal: components of ideal on ray class group generators
rubrics_metrics.description: Given bnr (from bnrinit(...,1)) and an ideal x, outputs a 2-component vector v where v[1] is the vector of components of x on the ray class group generators, and v[2] gives an integral-basis element α such that x = α·(product of generators) (?) (text shows relation). If flag = 0, output only v[1] and bnr need not contain generators. If x not coprime to modulus result undefined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN bnrisprincipal(GEN bnr, GEN x, long flag). Instead of numeric flags, use GEN isprincipalray(GEN bnr, GEN x) for flag = 0; request generators explicitly when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrrootnumber: compute Artin root number W(χ)
rubrics_metrics.description: If χ is a character over bnr (not necessarily primitive), returns the Artin root number W(χ) of modulus 1 satisfying Λ(1 − s, χ) = W(χ)Λ(s, χ) where Λ is the enlarged L-function. Generators of ray class group are needed; set flag = 1 if character is known primitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN bnrrootnumber(GEN bnr, GEN chi, long flag, long prec). Example usage given; requires bnr.gen to be present.

rubrics_metrics.name: bnrstark: compute relative equation(s) for class field using Stark units
rubrics_metrics.description: Finds a relative equation for the class field corresponding to the modulus in bnr and given congruence subgroup. Main variable of bnr must not be x, ground and class fields must be totally real. For base field Q, galoissubcyclo is used. The routine uses Stark units and requires a suitable auxiliary conductor; when class field not cyclic auxiliary conductor may not exist and bnrstark may return a vector of polynomials whose compositum is the requested field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN bnrstark(GEN bnr, GEN subgroup = NULL, long prec). If computation impossible or coefficients too large, try rnfkummer. The user may need to take compositum manually when multiple polynomials are returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: dirzetak: Dedekind zeta Dirichlet series coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives as a vector the first b coefficients of the Dedekind zeta function of number field nf considered as a Dirichlet series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN dirzetak(GEN nf, GEN b).

rubrics_metrics.name: factornf (deprecated): use nffactor
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete function for factorization of univariate polynomial x over number field defined by t. Algorithm reduces to factorization over Q (Trager’s trick). Main variable of t must be of lower priority than that of x; if coefficients involve non-rational number field elements, variable of these polmods must be same as main variable of t. Produces errors on inconsistent data or incorrect variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nffactor instead. Library syntax: GEN polfnf(GEN x, GEN t).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisexport: export Galois group to GAP/Magma permutation string
rubrics_metrics.description: Export the underlying permutation group of a Galois group gal (from galoisinit) as a string suitable for GAP (no flags or flag=0) or Magma (flag=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN galoisexport(GEN gal, long flag). Example shows use to compute IdGroup in GAP by piping string to gap -q.

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisfixedfield: compute fixed field of permutation/subgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Given gal (from galoisinit) and perm (an element, vector, or subgroup), compute the fixed field of gal by the automorphism(s) defined by perm acting on gal.roots. If no flags or flag=0, output [P,x] such that P defines the fixed field and x is a root expressed as a polmod in gal.pol. If flag=1 return only P. If flag=2 return [P,x,F] with F the factorization of gal.pol over field defined by P; variable v (default y) denotes root variable and must have proper priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN galoisfixedfield(GEN gal, GEN perm, long flag, long v = -1). Flag controls verbosity/extra factorization output; watch variable priority (Section 2.5.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisgetpol: query galpol database for polynomial with desired Galois group
rubrics_metrics.description: Query galpol package for a polynomial with Galois group isomorphic to GAP4(a,b), totally real if s=1 (default), totally complex if s=2. Output is [pol, den] where pol is the polynomial of degree a and den is denominator for nfgaloisconj speedup. If b and s omitted, returns number of isomorphism classes of groups of order a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN galoisgetpol(long a, long b, long s). Passing den to galoisinit or nfgaloisconj can speed computations. galoisnbpol(long a) available when b and s omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisidentify: identify isomorphism class of abstract group
rubrics_metrics.description: Output the isomorphism class of the underlying abstract group as [o, i] where o = group order and i = group index in GAP4 Small Group library. Limited to degree ≤ 127 (some larger easy orders supported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN galoisidentify(GEN gal). For larger groups use galoisexport and GAP to identify.

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisinit: compute Galois group for pol if 'weakly super-solvable'
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Galois group and necessary info for fixed fields of Galois extension K/Q where K is defined by pol. The extension must be Galois with Galois group 'weakly' super-solvable (existence of normal series with cyclic quotients except possibly final quotient A4 or S4), otherwise returns 0. Outputs 8-component vector gal with detailed components: gal[1]=pol, gal[2]=[p,e,q] p-adic modulus info, gal[3]=p-adic roots, gal[4]=inverse Vandermonde*gal[5], gal[5]=denominator multiple, gal[6]=G as permutations, gal[7]=generators, gal[8]=relative orders of generators. Various properties about generator orders in A4/S4 cases and unique expression of group elements as product of generators with exponents less than corresponding relative orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN galoisinit(GEN pol, GEN den = NULL). den must be suitable for gal[5] if present. The algorithm is an improved Allombert method. Many downstream galoisxxx routines require galoisinit output.

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisisabelian: test abelian and return HNF if requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Return 0 if gal is not abelian; if fl = 0 return the HNF matrix of gal over gal.gen; if fl = 1 return 1. Accepts subgroups returned by galoissubgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN galoisisabelian(GEN gal, long flag). Use for checking abelian property and obtaining HNF decomposition over generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: galoisisnormal: normal subgroup test
rubrics_metrics.description: Return 1 if subgrp is a normal subgroup of gal, else return 0. Accepts subgroups from galoissubgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long galoisisnormal(GEN gal, GEN subgrp).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoispermtopol: permutation to polynomial automorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: Given gal and a permutation perm (element of gal.group), return the polynomial defining the Galois automorphism (as output by nfgaloisconj) attached to perm. If perm is vector/matrix, apply recursively to all components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: galoisinit(pol); galoispermtopol(G, G[6])~ is equivalent to nfgaloisconj(pol) for degree ≥ 2. Library syntax: GEN galoispermtopol(GEN gal, GEN perm).

rubrics_metrics.name: galoissubcyclo: subextensions of cyclotomic fields / Kronecker-Weber generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the subextension of Q(ζ_n) fixed by subgroup H ⊂ (Z/nZ)^*. Parameters N and H can be given in several formats (N integer, output of znstar(n), or bnrinit output). Behavior depends on fl: fl=0 compute polynomial pol in variable v; fl=1 compute conductor (module); fl=2 output [pol, N].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN galoissubcyclo(GEN N, GEN H = NULL, long fl, long v = -1). Use helper polsubcyclo to compute all subfields (optionally of exact degree d). Beware when infty places not dividing module H is relative to N.

rubrics_metrics.name: galoissubfields: enumerate subfields of Galois group
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs all subfields of the Galois group G as a vector by applying galoisfixedfield to all subgroups. Meaning of flag is same as for galoisfixedfield.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN galoissubfields(GEN G, long flag, long v = -1). Watch variable priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: galoissubgroups: enumerate subgroups representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs all subgroups of G as vectors [gen, orders], where gen is vector of permutations generating the subgroup and orders are the relative orders of generators. Cardinatity is product of relative orders. Such subgroup can be used in galoisisabelian, galoissubgroups, galoisexport, galoisidentify. To get fixed field of subgroup sub, use galoisfixedfield(gal, sub[1]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN galoissubgroups(GEN G).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealadd: sum of two ideals in HNF and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum of two ideals x and y in number field nf; result given in HNF. Assumes arguments are ideals; cannot be used to add arbitrary Z-modules (will error).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealadd(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y). To add arbitrary Z-modules use mathnf(concat(A,B)). Examples show typical usage and errors for non-ideal inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealaddtoone: find Bézout combination for coprime ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two coprime integral ideals x and y, outputs [a,b] such that a ∈ x, b ∈ y and a + b = 1. Alternative syntax idealaddtoone(nf, v) accepts k-component vector of ideals summing to ZK and returns k-component vector e with e[i] ∈ x[i] and sum(e)=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealaddtoone0(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y = NULL). Useful for explicit Bézout relations in rings of integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealappr: approximate generator matching ideal valuations
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is a fractional ideal, gives element α in nf such that for all prime ideals p with non-zero valuation in x, vp(α) = vp(x), and vp(α) ≥ 0 for all other p. x may be given as prime ideal factorization with zero exponents allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument flag is deprecated and ignored. Library syntax: GEN idealappr(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealchinese: Chinese remainder for ideals with optional sign conditions and reuse structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Given x (prime ideal factorization) and y (vector of elements indexed by ideals in x), computes b such that vp(b - y_p) ≥ vp(x) for all primes in x and vp(b) ≥ 0 for all other p. x may be augmented as [x, s] where s is vector of signs for real embeddings, imposing sign conditions. If y omitted, returns a structure usable to solve many problems for same x more efficiently; that structure can be reused and further modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealchinese(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y = NULL). Use idealchineseinit when y = NULL for initialization. Examples show performance advantage of reuse and sign overrides.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealcoprime: make ideal coprime to another
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two integral ideals x and y, returns β in the field such that β·x is an integral ideal coprime to y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealcoprime(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealdiv / idealdivexact: quotient of ideals and flag for integral quotient
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotient x·y^{-1} of two ideals in nf, result in HNF. If flag non-zero, the quotient is assumed integral which can be much faster when quotient norm is small even if x and y norms are large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealdiv0(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y, long flag). Also available GEN idealdiv(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y) and GEN idealdivexact(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y) for flag variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealfactor: factor ideal into prime ideal powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors ideal x into prime ideal powers in nf. Output format is similar to factor; prime ideals are represented as output by idealprimedec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealfactor(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealfactorback: reconstruct ideal from factorization and optional reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives back the ideal corresponding to a factorization f; integer 1 corresponds to empty factorization. If e present, pairs (f[i], e[i]) produce product of f[i]^{e[i]}. If flag non-zero perform ideal reductions (idealred) along the way, useful for extended ideals so principal parts extracted by idealred are not lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealfactorback(GEN nf, GEN f, GEN e = NULL, long flag). Examples show reconstructing ideals and recovering principal generators via nffactorback.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealfrobenius: Frobenius permutation for unramified prime
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming K/Q Galois with gal = galoisinit(nf) and pr an unramified prime ideal in prid format, returns a permutation of gal.group defining the Frobenius element Frob_p attached to p. If p is unique prime number in pr, Frob(x) ≡ x^p mod p for x ∈ ZK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealfrobenius(GEN nf, GEN gal, GEN pr). Example: for cyclotomic field polcyclo(31), idealfrobenius maps to exponent congruence mod 31.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealhnf: Hermite normal form for ideal uZK + vZK and input conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives HNF of ideal uZK + vZK where u and v are elements of K. If v omitted returns HNF of ideal defined by u, where u may be algebraic number, maximal ideal, or matrix of column generators. Matrix input interpreted differently depending on number of columns (<N means ZK-module generated; ≥N treated as Z-basis of ideal). For quadratic fields allow u = Qfb(a,b,c) provided b^2 - 4ac = DK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealhnf0(GEN nf, GEN u, GEN v = NULL). Use idealhnf(GEN nf, GEN a) wrapper. Watch for incorrect variable/inputs (errors shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealintersect: intersection of two ideals (HNF) and Z-module intersection advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Intersection of ideals A and B in nf; result in HNF. Does not apply to general Z-modules (arguments replaced by ideals they generate). To intersect general Z-modules given by integer matrices, use provided ZM_intersect script which computes integral kernel-based intersection then mathnf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealintersect(GEN nf, GEN A, GEN B).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealinv: inverse of ideal with extended-ideal handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Inverse of ideal x in nf, given in HNF. If x is an extended ideal [I,t], inverting yields [I^{-1}, 1/t] updating principal part accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealinv(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: ideallist: list ideals up to given norm bound and flag options
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes list of all ideals of norm ≤ bound in nf. Output is row vector with exactly bound components, each a row vector containing info about ideals of a given norm depending on flag value: flag=0 give bid attached to ideals without generators; 1 include generators in bid; 2 requires nf bnf with units and returns [bid, U] where U discrete logs of units (for bnrclassnolist/bnrdisclist use); 3 as 2 but include generators; 4 give only HNF of ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ideallist0(GEN nf, long bound, long flag). Use ideallistarch to add Archimedean places. Examples show interpreting bids and using flag to obtain additional structural info like (Z_K/I)^*.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideallistarch: add Archimedean places to ideallist output
rubrics_metrics.description: Given list as output by ideallist (flag 0..3), and arch (ramified Archimedean places), return vector of vectors with same finite-part ordering but with archimedean component set to arch. Returned information type matches input flag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ideallistarch(GEN nf, GEN list, GEN arch). Adding t places at infinity adds t copies of Z/2Z to (Z_K/f)^*. Use when analyzing ray class groups with infinite places; shown interaction with bnrclassnolist and bnrdisclist.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideallog: discrete logarithm of element relative to idealstar bid generators
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute discrete logarithm of x (element of nf, may be non-integral but must have valuation 0 at primes in support of D) on generators given in bid.gen. If generators gi have orders di, returns column vector xi with 0 ≤ xi < di such that x ≡ ∏ g_i^{xi} (mod *D). When nf omitted treat as rationals (x must be t_INT and bid from idealstar(,N)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ideallog(GEN nf = NULL, GEN x, GEN bid). Limitations of discrete log algorithms apply when D contains infinite places; Zideallog available when nf is NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealmin (deprecated): use idealred
rubrics_metrics.description: Idealmin computes a pseudo-minimum of ideal x in direction vdir — function is useless and kept for backward compatibility. Use idealred instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealmin(GEN nf, GEN ix, GEN vdir = NULL). Prefer idealred.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealmul and variants: multiply ideals and extended-ideal principal part updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideal multiplication x*y in nf returns HNF product. If either operand is extended [I,t], principal parts combined: [I,t]*[J,u] -> [IJ, tu]; I*[J,u] -> [IJ, u]. If flag non-zero, reduce result using idealred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealmul0(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y, long flag). Also available: GEN idealmul(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y) (flag=0) and GEN idealmulred(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y) (flag ≠ 0).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealnorm: norm of ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the norm of ideal x in nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealnorm(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealnumden: numerator/denominator ideal decomposition of element
rubrics_metrics.description: Return [A,B] where A and B are coprime integer ideals such that x = A/B in nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealnumden(GEN nf, GEN x). Example: idealnumden(K,(x+1)/2) returns integer ideal numerator and denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealp ow: raise ideal to integer power and reduction option
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute k-th power of ideal x (k ∈ Z). If x is extended [I,t], raising yields [I^k, t^k]. If flag non-zero, reduce result using idealred throughout binary powering process (not same as powering then reducing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealpow0(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN k, long flag). Also available: GEN idealpow(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN k) and GEN idealpows(GEN nf, GEN x, long k) (flag=0). GEN idealpowred corresponds to flag=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: idealprimedec: prime ideal decomposition of rational prime
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute prime ideal decomposition of prime number p in number field K represented by nf. Returns vector of prid structures pr = [p, a, e, f, mb] where a is an algebraic integer so p = pZ_K + aZ_K, e ramification index, f residual index, mb multiplication table attached to algebraic integer b used to compute valuations. The algebraic number a is guaranteed to have valuation 1 at the prime ideal (automatic if e > 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN idealprimedec(GEN nf, GEN p, GEN f = 0) where optional f restricts to primes of residue degree ≤ f. Access members by pr.p, pr.e, pr.f, pr.gen, etc. If non-prime p given result undefined.
